label: input token i early in the original phase (t<=3)
explanation: Fires almost entirely (98% of mass) in the original phase at positions t=0..3, mainly when the input token is the letter i (72% of mass, 21x lift); n is a weaker secondary trigger (17% of mass, 5.5x), with small contributions from 0, s, f, o, a. Essentially silent from t>=4 and in the delimiter/copy phases, and on repeated occurrences of a token (in_first=0). i at t=0 always fires (precision 1.0) but weakly; strongest activations are i at t=2 after prefixes like k m, k 2, k o, 2 m (t=2 holds 45% of mass). Whether i at t=1..3 fires depends on preceding tokens: prefixes containing f, l, z, v, s, h, x, d, a tend to suppress it (excluding them raises precision to ~0.88 but costs recall). Predicate: i at t<=3 gives dev F1 0.64, mass recall 0.71; adding n raises mass recall to 0.88 but halves precision.
